card_01DUE.title: [devflow] Brief: Due dates on tasks
card_01DUE.body:
## Brief
- Goal: a task can have a due date, and `tasks list --overdue` shows the open tasks whose due date has passed.
- For whom: people who track their own work with `tasks` in the terminal.
- Success: `tasks add "pay rent" --due 2026-11-01`, then `tasks list --overdue` run on 2026-11-02 lists it; `make test` is green.
- Out of scope: reminders and notifications; recurring tasks; times and time zones (dates only).
- Constraints: the output of `tasks list` and `tasks show` stays the same for tasks without a due date.
- Decisions: dates are ISO (YYYY-MM-DD); a task without a due date is never overdue.

## Context
### Facts
- A task is a dataclass with id, title, list and done, serialized by `to_dict`/`from_dict` (`src/tasks/model.py:5`).
- The store loads and saves the whole JSON file on every command (`src/tasks/store.py:12`, `docs/adr/0001-one-json-file-store.md`).
- `add` and `list` parse their options by hand inside `main()` (`src/tasks/cli.py:8`).
- `tasks list` prints `[ ] <id>  <title>  (<list>)` per task (`src/tasks/cli.py:58`); `tasks show` prints one field per line (`src/tasks/cli.py:70`).
### Test seam
- `main(argv, store, out)` with a store under `tmp_path`, exercised by `tests/test_cli.py`; the store alone by `tests/test_store.py`.
### Commands
- test: `make test` (`Makefile:1`), which runs `python3 -m pytest -q`.
### Boundaries
- Always: run `make test` before done (`AGENTS.md`).
- Ask first: changing where or how tasks are stored (`AGENTS.md`).
- Never: change the output of `tasks list` or `tasks show` without a flag (`AGENTS.md`).
### Assumptions I'm making
1. "Today" comes from the system date, and tests inject it.
2. A task saved before this change has no `due` key, which means no due date.
### Not confirmed
- No git history in this checkout.
### Glossary and ADRs
- `CONTEXT.md`: added **Due date** and **Overdue**.

card_01REN.title: [devflow] Brief: Lists become projects
card_01REN.body:
## Brief
- Goal: the "list" concept is called "project" everywhere a person sees it: the `--list` option becomes `--project`, `tasks list` and `tasks show` say project, and the JSON field `list` becomes `project`.
- For whom: people who use `tasks`; "list" clashes with the `tasks list` command.
- Success: `tasks add "x" --project home`, then `tasks list --project home` lists it; no command, test or doc uses "list" for the concept; `make test` is green.
- Out of scope: nested projects; moving tasks between projects in bulk.
- Constraints: people's shell scripts call `tasks add --list X`, and their `~/.tasks.json` files hold a `list` field. Both keep working while the change rolls out, and for one release after the new names ship.
- Decisions: one release accepts both `--list` and `--project` and reads both fields, writing only `project`; the release after removes `--list` and the `list` field.

## Context
### Facts
- The concept appears in the model field `list` (`src/tasks/model.py:8`), `Store.add(list_name)` (`src/tasks/store.py:25`), eleven places in `main()` (`src/tasks/cli.py`), both test files, `README.md` and `CONTEXT.md`.
- Old JSON files are read by `Task.from_dict` (`src/tasks/model.py:15`).
### Test seam
- `main(argv, store, out)`, exercised by `tests/test_cli.py`; reading old files by `tests/test_store.py`.
### Commands
- test: `make test` (`Makefile:1`).
### Boundaries
- Always: run `make test` before done (`AGENTS.md`).
- Ask first: changing how tasks are stored (`AGENTS.md`).
- Never: break the output people's scripts parse (`AGENTS.md`).
### Assumptions I'm making
1. `tasks list --list X` is renamed too, to `tasks list --project X`.
### Not confirmed
- How many people's scripts parse `(list)` in the output.
### Glossary and ADRs
- none

card_01TAG.title: [devflow] Brief: Tags on tasks
card_01TAG.body:
## Brief
- Goal: a task can carry tags, and `tasks list --tag <tag>` shows only the open tasks with that tag.
- For whom: people who track their own work with `tasks`.
- Success: `tasks add "renew passport" --tag errands --tag gov`, then `tasks list --tag errands` lists it and nothing else, and `tasks show` prints its tags; `make test` is green.
- Out of scope: tag colours; renaming tags; tags on lists.
- Decisions: a task has zero or more tags; tags are lowercase words; `--tag` can repeat.

## Context
### Facts
- `main()` parses every command's options by hand, in one if/elif chain with index arithmetic per command (`src/tasks/cli.py:8-85`). A new option means a new branch in each command that takes it, plus its own "needs a value" error.
- `--tag` is needed by both `add` and `list`, and `show` prints a new line.
- A task is a dataclass serialized by `to_dict`/`from_dict` (`src/tasks/model.py:5`).
### Test seam
- `main(argv, store, out)`, exercised by `tests/test_cli.py`.
### Commands
- test: `make test` (`Makefile:1`).
### Boundaries
- Always: run `make test` before done (`AGENTS.md`).
- Ask first: changing how tasks are stored (`AGENTS.md`).
- Never: change the output of `tasks list` or `tasks show` without a flag (`AGENTS.md`).
### Assumptions I'm making
1. `argparse` is acceptable, since it is in the standard library.
2. Error messages for bad options may change wording, as no script parses them.
### Not confirmed
- No git history in this checkout.
### Glossary and ADRs
- `CONTEXT.md`: added **Tag**.
